newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba urges further efforts to cut Bonn's deficit.
newsitem.headline: Buba urges further efforts to cut Bonn's deficit.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that Bonn should make extra efforts to rein in its budget deficit, adding that unforeseen events could otherwise endanger the reaching of its budgetary goal for 1997.

Bonn is forecasting a budget deficit at 2.9 percent of gross domestic product for 1997, only marginally below the three percent level laid down in the Maastricht treaty as the desired maximum for countries entering monetary union.

The Bundesbank noted in its report that the prospects for this year's budget already looked less rosy than had been the case last autumn, given last year's tax deficits came in lower than expected and the recent rise in unemployment.

"It can also not be ruled out that further unexpected burdens on the budget may arise in the course of the year, whether on the income side or on particular types of expenditure," the Bundesbank said.

"In view of this position efforts are needed to achieve further savings," it said, adding that the reduction of the deficit was not only desirable with a view to Germany's qualification for Maastricht.
